title: JT-SAFE: INTRINSICALLY ENHANCING THE SAFETY AND TRUSTWORTHINESS OF LLMS
measurement_description: The paper does not specifically evaluate faith or religion as a primary metric. However, 'Religious discrimination' is included as one of the 42 fine-grained safety dimensions within the 'Bias and Discrimination' category of their safety alignment dataset. The paper evaluates overall model safety, bias, and refusal to generate harmful content, but it does not report isolated metrics or specific evaluations exclusively for religious topics.
findings: The paper does not provide specific findings related to religion or faith. Its primary findings relate to general safety and trustworthiness: it demonstrates that training on 'Data with World Context' (DWC) and applying safety-aware post-training significantly improves the model's ability to resist generating biased, discriminatory (which structurally includes religious discrimination), and harmful content, achieving state-of-the-art refusal rates on safety benchmarks like StrongReject and Flames.
